meta.title: Base64 to PDF Converter - Free Online Decoder & Download
meta.description: Free Base64 to PDF converter. Paste a Base64 string or data URI and download the decoded PDF instantly. 100% client-side, no upload needed.

tagline: Decode Base64 strings and download PDF files instantly — no upload required
pageDescription: Convert any Base64-encoded string to a PDF file directly in your browser — no server upload, no registration. Paste raw Base64 data or a data URI (data:application/pdf;base64,...) and download the decoded PDF in one click. Ideal for developers debugging REST API responses that return Base64 PDFs, handling email attachments encoded in Base64, testing document generation pipelines, and inspecting PDF files from data exports. Validates Base64 padding automatically, detects malformed input and previews the converted document before download.

instructions.title: How to use Base64 to PDF

steps.title: Paste your Base64 string
steps.description: Copy the Base64-encoded PDF string from your API response, email client or data source and paste it into the input field. You can paste raw Base64 or a full data URI starting with data:application/pdf;base64,

steps.title: Validate the Base64 input
steps.description: The tool automatically checks that the string is valid Base64 and contains a decodable PDF. If the input has missing padding characters (=) or invalid characters, an error message will guide you to fix it.

steps.title: Preview the decoded PDF
steps.description: Once validated, click Convert to PDF. The tool decodes the string and shows a full PDF preview using your browser's built-in viewer. Check that the document looks correct before downloading.

steps.title: Download the PDF file
steps.description: Click the Download PDF button to save the decoded file to your device. The filename is auto-generated with today's date (document_YYYY-MM-DD.pdf) or you can set a custom name before converting. No data is sent to any server.

proTips: If your string starts with data:application/pdf;base64, paste it as-is — the tool strips the header automatically
Missing = padding at the end of the string is the most common cause of decode errors — add one or two = characters at the end to fix it
For very large Base64 strings (over 5MB), paste in chunks to verify which segment is corrupted
Use the browser console (F12) to copy Base64 strings from API responses directly
If the PDF preview appears blank or shows a password prompt, the source file may be password-protected or was corrupted before encoding
troubleshooting: Invalid Base64 characters: Remove whitespace, line breaks or non-Base64 characters from your string
Missing padding error: Add one or two = characters at the end of the string until the error clears
Blank or corrupt PDF after download: The original file was likely corrupted before being encoded — verify the source
Data URI not recognized: Ensure the format includes a comma separator (e.g. data:application/pdf;base64,...) — any MIME type is supported as long as the Base64 payload follows the comma
Very slow processing: Base64 strings over 10MB may take a few seconds — this is normal for large PDF files
